title: Evidence Analysis
instructions: Analyze the laptop image, memory dump, and network logs. Each artifact points to the same suspect.

messages.text: Three artifacts, one operator. Open the case file and let the evidence answer.

notify.text: Memory holds what disk forgot. Find the process that spawned the payload.
notify.speaker: instructor

notify.text: Logs show the exfil path - destination first, then volume.
notify.speaker: instructor

rubric.label: Identify suspicious files on the laptop
Extract the hidden string from the memory dump

briefing.narrative: The forensic image, memory dump, and network logs from the rogue laptop are now available. Analyze the three artifacts in the Evidence panel to find the malware, the hidden handle, and the exfiltration target.
briefing.speaker: instructor

choices.text: Open the evidence and begin analysis

laptop_analysis.narrative: The laptop inventory lists the files on the imaged C: drive. Look for the file that does not belong on a standard system.
laptop_analysis.speaker: instructor

choices.text: C2_client.exe in Downloads is the suspicious file
choices.feedback: Correct. The executable and a temp exfil log were added outside normal system files.
notepad.exe is a normal Windows binary. The custom C2_client.exe is the anomaly.

memory_analysis.narrative: The memory dump contains running process data. Examine the hex and find the hidden string that identifies the operator behind the malware.
memory_analysis.speaker: instructor

choices.feedback: Correct. The ASCII/hex for 'Aberr4ti0n' is embedded in the process memory.

choices.text: No usable strings are present in the dump
choices.feedback: The dump does contain a string. Look at the right-hand ASCII panel in the hex view.

network_analysis.narrative: The packet logs capture network activity around the time of the incident. Identify the external destination receiving data from the rogue host.
network_analysis.speaker: instructor

choices.feedback: Correct. Multiple TLS connections from the rogue host uploaded several megabytes to 203.0.113.55.

choices.text: All traffic is internal and benign
choices.feedback: There are large outbound TLS uploads to an external IP.

complete.narrative: The analysis is complete. The laptop contained C2 malware, the operator handle is Aberr4ti0n, and the exfiltration target is 203.0.113.55. You are ready to write the forensic report.
complete.speaker: instructor
